Don’t guess at motive. Check the gap.

Confidence is a style. Support is a relationship you can inspect. These four moves keep the conclusion tied to the record.

  1. 01

    Claim

    Pin down the exact statement. Confidence, fluency and tone are not evidence.

  2. 02

    Required evidence

    Decide what would have to be visible for that statement to hold.

  3. 03

    Observed record

    Read what is present, conflicting or still missing—without filling the gaps.

  4. 04

    Finding

    Name only the relationship the record supports. Keep intent separate.

06 cases

Six synthetic cases. One habit to reuse.

The evidence shape changes: a missing file, an incomplete denominator, a citation mismatch, the wrong identity, an unknown external result, and one supported control. The rule does not.

  1. 01Missing outputThe missing fileAn AI system says it created a required file. The reviewed revision contains no file at that path.×ContradictedClaimed output missing
  2. 02Uncounted casesThe reassuring average with missing casesAn audit reports a reassuring average while failed, unscored or unavailable cases are absent from the headline.?Insufficient evidenceUnaccounted evaluation cases · Decision-relevant omission
  3. 03Unsupported citationThe citation that does not support the answerAn answer provides a source link, but the supplied source states a different fact from the answer.×ContradictedCitation does not support claim
  4. 04Wrong identityThe claim attached to the wrong product identityA capability statement for one product version or service surface is presented as if it applies to another.×ContradictedProduct or version mismatch
  5. 05Unknown external resultThe lost response after a consequential actionA tool call times out after sending a consequential request, so the system cannot tell whether the action failed or succeeded.?Insufficient evidenceExternal result unknown
  6. 06Supported controlA supported revision-bound claimA bounded claim names its passing check, exact reviewed Git revision and touched paths, and the repository state matches the record.✓SupportedSupported control
Boundary

What this record can show—and what it cannot.

A useful result says exactly how far the evidence reaches, then stops.

  • Six visibly synthetic casesTeaching examples, not a prevalence estimate or allegation about a real incident.
  • One deterministic ruleThe browser and local checker import the same classifier.
  • Exact public revisionsEvery source keeps its revision and reviewed-through date beside the claim.
  • No hidden collectionNo account, analytics, tracker, backend or live model receives your choices.

If the record is wrong, show the smallest thing that changes it.

Run the checker, inspect an exact revision, or bring a public-safe counterexample. Corrigibility is part of the method.
